 Blow Away Hunger helping out busy holiday season for Carlyle and District Food Bank
 Scott Boulton, 
 DiscoverEstevan.com | 
 Thursday, Nov 19 2026, 10:28 AM 
 Share: 
 Copied! 
 The Food Bank often serves around 70 people a month, with the holidays seeing an increase. (Photo courtesy of Elyse Mantei) 
 Article continues below advertisement ↴ 
 The Carlyle and District Food Bank has distributed more than 70 food hampers over the past two days, with more help from the community coming thanks to Blow Away Hunger taking place today.
 From 8 a.m. to 9 p.m., food and monetary donations are being accepted at Southern Plains Co-op grocery stores in Estevan, Carlyle, and Oxbow.
 The Oxbow location is supporting both the Carnduff & District Food Bank (food donations) and Oxbow Community Emergency Support (monetary donations), while Estevan supports the local Salvation Army Food Bank.
 Chairperson Theresa Luedtke says Carlyle's food bank has been busy, with its annual support programs receiving strong backing from the surrounding communities.
 The local community has already been giving donations to the food bank, according to Luedtke. 
 "It's been great so far; last night I picked up a full Tahoe load of bags," said Luedtke, thanking community members for their generosity.
 Food bank demand remains steady
 The food bank typically distributes between 60 and 70 hampers each month throughout Carlyle and the surrounding district.
 Luedtke says demand has remained relatively consistent, although she expects the number of hampers distributed to climb above 100 next month.
 The organization also supports several other initiatives throughout its service area, including providing snacks to schools and helping libraries in four communities ensure children have something to eat when they visit.
 While food hampers remain the food bank's primary service, Luedtke says those additional programs are becoming an increasingly important part of its work.

 Community support makes the difference
 Luedtke says the organization is grateful for the support it receives from individuals, service clubs and local businesses.
 "We just can't thank people enough for all the support that we get," she said.
 As the holiday season approaches, Luedtke says the food bank expects its usual seasonal increase in demand and encourages community members to continue supporting local efforts to address food insecurity.
 "The community and the service clubs and the companies that support us, we couldn't do it without their support," said Luedtke.
 More information on how you can support the cause is available on the Blow Away Hunger 2026 event page .
